title: How the threat of disease has shaped human behavior, with Mark Schaller, PhD

sentences.en: Although we are currently in the midst of a global pandemic,
sentences.zh: 尽管我们目前正处于全球大流行之中，

sentences.en: we should not forget that we are fortunate to live in a time where we have vaccines and other public health measures we can take to avoid illnesses such as polio, smallpox,
sentences.zh: 但我们不应忘记，我们很幸运生活在一个拥有疫苗和其他公共卫生措施的时代，可以避免脊髓灰质炎、天花、

sentences.en: cholera, even bubonic plague, and we hope that soon COVID-19 will be vanquished by vaccines.
sentences.zh: 霍乱，甚至是鼠疫等疾病，我们希望新冠肺炎（COVID-19）也能很快被疫苗所战胜。

sentences.en: But for our ancestors, infectious diseases were a constant danger, so much so that the threat of infection has actually helped shape human evolution.
sentences.zh: 但对于我们的祖先来说，传染病是一种持续的威胁，以至于这种感染威胁实际上已经帮助塑造了人类的进化。

sentences.en: Disgust, wariness of strangers, cultural norms around food and cleanliness, all of these behaviors may have evolved, at least in part, to keep us safe from infectious disease.
sentences.zh: 厌恶感、对陌生人的警惕、围绕食物和清洁的文化规范，所有这些行为的进化，至少在一定程度上，是为了保护我们免受传染病的侵害。

sentences.en: Researchers call this suite of protective mechanisms the behavioral immune system,
sentences.zh: 研究人员将这一套保护机制称为“行为免疫系统”，

sentences.en: but are the defenses that humans evolved thousands of years ago to ward off infection suitable to protect us from the diseases we face today?
sentences.zh: 但人类几千年前进化出的防御感染的防御机制，是否足以保护我们免受当今所面临疾病的侵害呢？

sentences.en: Do they do more harm than good in some cases?
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，它们是否弊大于利？

sentences.en: And what is the role of disgust in keeping us safe and healthy?
sentences.zh: 厌恶感在保障我们安全和健康方面又扮演了什么角色？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听美国心理学会的旗舰播客《心理学谈话》，该节目探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯（Kim Mills）。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Mark Schaller, a professor of psychology at the University of British Columbia.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是英属哥伦比亚大学心理学教授马克·沙勒（Mark Schaller）博士。

sentences.en: Dr. Schaller coined the term behavioral immune system, and he studies how the perceived threat of disease has shaped human psychology.
sentences.zh: 沙勒博士创造了“行为免疫系统”这一术语，他研究感知的疾病威胁如何塑造了人类心理。

sentences.en: He's also interested more broadly in human social cognition, stereotyping, evolutionary psychology, and cultural psychology.
sentences.zh: 他还对更广泛的人类社会认知、刻板印象、进化心理学和文化心理学感兴趣。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us today, Dr. Schaller.
sentences.zh: 感谢您今天参加我们的节目，沙勒博士。

sentences.en: Hey, thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 嘿，谢谢你们邀请我。

sentences.en: I'm delighted to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Let's start with a broad question.
sentences.zh: 让我们从一个宏观的问题开始。

sentences.en: What exactly is the behavioral immune system, and how and why did it evolve?
sentences.zh: 究竟什么是行为免疫系统？它是如何进化的，又为何进化？

sentences.en: The behavioral immune system, I think, can be kind of thought of as a suite of psychological responses that evolve to help defend against the threat of infectious diseases.
sentences.zh: 我认为，行为免疫系统可以被看作是一套为了帮助抵御传染病威胁而进化出来的心理反应机制。

sentences.en: And it's comprised of psychological mechanisms that help us detect potentially infectious things in the immediate environment to respond to those things in a way that might help us avoid them and therefore to help keep us from getting sick.
sentences.zh: 它由一系列心理机制组成，帮助我们检测环境中潜在的传染源，并以可能有助于我们避开它们的方式做出反应，从而帮助我们避免生病。

sentences.en: The second part of your question, why do we even have this set of mechanisms?
sentences.zh: 关于你问题的第二部分，我们为什么会有这套机制？

sentences.en: When I think of this, I think of it useful to think about the benefits as well as the costs of what we might think of as the real immune system.
sentences.zh: 当我思考这个问题时，我认为考虑我们所谓的“真实免疫系统”的收益和成本是很有用的。

sentences.en: You know, our immunological defenses against infections kick in when those things, bacteria, viruses, whatever, when they get inside us.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们针对感染的免疫防御系统会在细菌、病毒等进入我们体内时启动。

sentences.en: And it's awesome that we have these immunological defenses that can mount a defense against those things.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有能够针对这些病原体建立防御的免疫系统，这太棒了。

sentences.en: But it's hugely costly.
sentences.zh: 但它的代价非常巨大。

sentences.en: And to actually mount an immunological defense against bacteria and so forth, it consumes an enormous amount of caloric resources.
sentences.zh: 为了真正建立起针对细菌等的免疫防御，它会消耗大量的热量资源。

sentences.en: It can be debilitating.
sentences.zh: 这可能会让人变得虚弱。

sentences.en: It prevents us from doing all kinds of other things.
sentences.zh: 它会阻碍我们做各种其他事情。

sentences.en: So, in a sense, I think you can think of what we call our immune system as kind of like medical insurance.
sentences.zh: 所以，在某种意义上，我认为你可以把我们所谓的免疫系统看作是一种医疗保险。

sentences.en: It's great to have, but it really stinks when we have to use it.
sentences.zh: 拥有它很好，但真的要用到它时，感觉就很糟糕了。

sentences.en: It'd be better not to have to use it at all.
sentences.zh: 最好根本不需要用到它。

sentences.en: And that's where the behavioral immune system comes into play.
sentences.zh: 这就是行为免疫系统发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: It's a kind of a form of preventative medicine.
sentences.zh: 它是一种预防医学的形式。

sentences.en: These mechanisms help prevent us from having to actually mount that costly immunological defense and so serves as kind of a complementary kind of defense against the threat of infectious diseases.
sentences.zh: 这些机制有助于防止我们不得不真正建立那种昂贵的免疫防御，因此它作为一种针对传染病威胁的补充性防御手段。

sentences.en: You found that one of the biggest implications of this system is how it affects our interactions with other people, particularly people who are different from us in some way.
sentences.zh: 你发现该系统最大的影响之一是它如何影响我们与他人的互动，特别是与我们在某些方面不同的人的互动。

sentences.en: What is the relationship between the behavioral immune system and prejudice or xenophobia?
sentences.zh: 行为免疫系统与偏见或仇外心理之间有什么关系？

sentences.en: Generally speaking, when people are more concerned about the threat of disease, if they feel more vulnerable to infection,
sentences.zh: 总的来说，当人们更担心疾病威胁时，如果他们感到更容易受到感染，

sentences.en: they tend to respond more harshly to people who look different, to people who act different, to strangers, to people who they perceive as being from strange or different places.
sentences.zh: 他们往往会对长相不同的人、行为不同的人、陌生人，以及他们认为来自陌生或不同地方的人做出更严厉的反应。

sentences.en: And there's a couple of different reasons why that might be.
sentences.zh: 这背后有几个不同的原因。

sentences.en: One is this idea that historically people from who are strange or from strange different places might have been more likely to bring with them more exotic parasites,
sentences.zh: 其一是这种观点：从历史上看，来自陌生或奇怪地方的人更有可能携带更多外来的寄生虫，

sentences.en: things that are more likely to make us sick.
sentences.zh: 那些更容易让我们生病的东西。

sentences.en: And that might be possible, but I actually think a less obvious answer is probably a more compelling answer to the question,
sentences.zh: 这可能是可能的，但我实际上认为一个不那么明显的答案可能对这个问题更有说服力，

sentences.en: which has to do with the fact that a lot of the things that people historically have done in order to avoid infection had to do with doing things a certain way.
sentences.zh: 这与这样一个事实有关：人们历史上为了避免感染所做的许多事情，都与以某种特定方式做事有关。

sentences.en: We prepare food a certain way, we have these norms of hygiene,
sentences.zh: 我们以特定的方式准备食物，我们有这些卫生规范，

sentences.en: and we have norms that govern what are appropriate ways of engaging in intimate interpersonal contact with other folks.
sentences.zh: 我们还有规范来管理与他人进行亲密人际接触的适当方式。

sentences.en: So we have these rituals and norms, and prior to contemporary technological advances in medicine and pharmacology and public health,
sentences.zh: 所以我们有这些仪式和规范，在当代医学、药理学和公共卫生技术进步之前，

sentences.en: these kind of rituals and norms were kind of most of what people had to help them figure out how to avoid coming into contact with infectious diseases.
sentences.zh: 这些仪式和规范几乎是人们所拥有的全部，用来帮助他们弄清楚如何避免接触传染病。

sentences.en: Which means that anybody who is likely to do things differently, which means that anybody who is likely to violate those norms, to do things differently,
sentences.zh: 这意味着任何可能以不同方式做事的人，也就是任何可能违反这些规范、以不同方式做事的人，

sentences.en: to violate norms of sanitation and hygiene, they posed a threat not just to themselves, but to anybody in the community.
sentences.zh: 违反卫生规范的人，不仅对自己构成了威胁，也对社区中的任何人构成了威胁。

sentences.en: So people who seem likely to act differently, people who are from foreign lands, it may kind of activate the sense of these people don't do the things that we're likely to do.
sentences.zh: 所以，那些看起来行为不同的人，那些来自外国的人，可能会激活一种感觉，即“这些人不做我们通常做的事情”。

sentences.en: And so, getting back to your question, the idea is that this kind of xenophobic response to people who are different,
sentences.zh: 所以，回到你的问题，这个想法是，这种对不同人群的仇外反应，

sentences.en: maybe have historically served the function of trying to avoid and keep away people who would violate local rituals and social norMs.
sentences.zh: 在历史上可能起到了试图避免和远离那些会违反当地仪式和社会规范的人的功能。

sentences.en: So some of these things sound like they could be traditions, things that would be passed down from generation to generation, but was there something going way,
sentences.zh: 所以其中一些事情听起来像是传统，是代代相传的东西，但有没有什么东西可以追溯到很久很久以前，

sentences.en: way back that maybe the humans who prepared food in a certain way just tended to survive, and therefore, it got passed along in that way, almost like an instinctive thing?
sentences.zh: 也许那些以特定方式准备食物的人往往能存活下来，因此它以这种方式被传递下去，几乎像是一种本能的东西？

sentences.en: I wouldn't say an instinctive thing, but more of a kind of a superstitious thing.
sentences.zh: 我不会说这是一种本能，而更像是一种迷信的东西。

sentences.en: So food preparation is one of my favorite examples of this, because biologists who have studied spices have found that the use of culinary spices is a natural form of antibiotic.
sentences.zh: 食物准备是我最喜欢的例子之一，因为研究香料的生物学家发现，烹饪香料的使用是一种天然的抗生素。

sentences.en: It's not just hot peppers, but just about every kind of herb and spice that people use to flavor food actually has some antibacterial properties.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是辣椒，人们用来调味的几乎每一种草药和香料实际上都具有一定的抗菌特性。

sentences.en: And so, what's likely to have happened is that people just kind of, through trial and error, kind of figured out that, hey, if we prepare food in this kind of way, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，很可能发生的情况是，人们只是通过反复试验，发现，嘿，如果我们以这种方式准备食物，你知道，

sentences.en: we put hot spices on our meat, then people are less likely to get sick.
sentences.zh: 我们在肉上放热辣的香料，那么人们生病的可能性就更小。

sentences.en: Nobody really knew why, right?
sentences.zh: 没人真正知道为什么，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, way back when, before people even had a concept of germ theory.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在很久以前，在人们甚至还没有细菌理论概念的时候。

sentences.en: But, I mean, but, you know, you can figure out, all right, people get sick if we prepare food this way, and they don't if we prepare food this other way.
sentences.zh: 但是，我的意思是，你知道，你可以弄清楚，好吧，如果我们这样准备食物，人们就会生病，而如果我们用另一种方式准备，他们就不会生病。

sentences.en: And so, this kind of, it's like, well, let's do that.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就像是，好吧，让我们这样做。

sentences.en: Let's do the thing that keeps us from getting sick.
sentences.zh: 让我们做那些能让我们不生病的事情。

sentences.en: They might have had a whole mythology around that, but the idea is that they would for sure tend to teach their children.
sentences.zh: 他们可能围绕这一点有一整套神话，但想法是他们肯定会倾向于教导他们的孩子。

sentences.en: They would pass that on.
sentences.zh: 他们会把这些传下去。

sentences.en: And so, it becomes kind of a cultural norm without any necessary reason as to why it works.
sentences.zh: 因此，它变成了一种文化规范，而不需要任何关于它为什么有效的必然理由。

sentences.en: There would just be this sense, this superstitious sense of this is what works.
sentences.zh: 只会有一种感觉，一种迷信的感觉，即“这就是有效的方法”。

sentences.en: And so, folks who don't do that or seem likely not to do those things, people who seem likely to violate these norms, are viewed as threats.
sentences.zh: 所以，那些不这样做或看起来不太可能做这些事情的人，那些看起来可能违反这些规范的人，被视为威胁。

sentences.en: You've conducted some very interesting studies that suggest that feeling threatened by infectious disease can make people more conformist, more likely to follow rules.
sentences.zh: 你进行了一些非常有趣的研究，表明感到传染病威胁会使人变得更墨守成规，更可能遵守规则。

sentences.en: And you found this plays out both at the individual level, but at the societal level.
sentences.zh: 你发现这不仅在个人层面，而且在社会层面也发挥作用。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that research?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈那项研究吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that, I mean, that follows directly upon what we were just talking about.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这直接延续了我们刚才讨论的内容。

sentences.en: So, generally speaking, this tendency to be, to respond adversely to things that seem like they might pose some sort of threat of infection, whether it's, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，总的来说，这种倾向于对那些看起来可能构成某种感染威胁的事物做出不利反应的倾向，无论是，你知道，

sentences.en: some thing that actually seems immediately infectious, or some person who seems like they might be, pose a threat of violating norMs.
sentences.zh: 某种看起来立即具有传染性的事物，还是某个看起来可能构成违反规范威胁的人。

sentences.en: We tend to be hyper-sensitive to these perceived threats under circumstances in which we either are more vulnerable to infection or, for whatever reason,
sentences.zh: 在那些我们更容易受到感染，或者由于某种原因，

sentences.en: just kind of feel more vulnerable to infection.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是感到更容易受到感染的情况下，我们往往对这些感知的威胁过度敏感。

sentences.en: And so, in psychology experiments, experiments that I've done, experiments that other people have done,
sentences.zh: 所以，在心理学实验中，我做的实验，其他人做的实验，

sentences.en: we've used manipulations that temporarily just make people feel a little more freaked out by disease.
sentences.zh: 我们使用了操纵手段，暂时让人们对疾病感到更加恐慌。

sentences.en: And we find that when people do feel more freaked out by disease, they tend to be, to endorse more conformist attitudes.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，当人们确实对疾病感到更加恐慌时，他们往往会支持更墨守成规的态度。

sentences.en: They want other people to conform more.
sentences.zh: 他们希望其他人也更墨守成规。

sentences.en: And they also are more likely to conform themselves.
sentences.zh: 而且他们自己也更有可能墨守成规。

sentences.en: They are themselves less likely to violate norMs.
sentences.zh: 他们自己违反规范的可能性更小。

sentences.en: They're more likely to go along with majority opinion and so forth.
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能顺从多数人的意见等等。

sentences.en: So, that's kind of what's happening at an individual, at a psychological level of analysis.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是在个人、心理分析层面发生的事情。

sentences.en: But you do see this analogy at a much broader worldwide cultural level of analysis, too.
sentences.zh: 但你在更广泛的全球文化分析层面也能看到这种类比。

sentences.en: So, in some countries, simply because of meteorological variables and other sorts of things, some countries tend to just have more infectious diseases going around.
sentences.zh: 所以，在一些国家，仅仅因为气象变量和其他各种因素，一些国家往往会有更多的传染病流行。

sentences.en: And it turns out that in countries that have historically had more infectious diseases, people in general are more conformiSt.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，在历史上传染病较多的国家，人们普遍更墨守成规。

sentences.en: They're more likely to encourage obedience in children.
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能鼓励儿童服从。

sentences.en: They're more likely to conform to majority opinion themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们自己更有可能顺从多数人的意见。

sentences.en: They're more likely to do whatever they can to encourage, not just themselves, but folks around them, to uphold existing cultural traditions.
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能尽其所能去鼓励，不仅是他们自己，还有周围的人，去维护现有的文化传统。

sentences.en: So, you talked about meteorology playing a role here.
sentences.zh: 所以，你谈到了气象学在这里发挥的作用。

sentences.en: So, are you saying, for example, in the tropics, we always talk about all of these tropical diseases.
sentences.zh: 所以，你是说，例如，在热带地区，我们总是谈论所有这些热带疾病。

sentences.en: So, that's one of the places where weather would be playing this role.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是天气发挥这种作用的地方之一。

sentences.en: Whereas, if you live in the Arctic, where it's cold and the germs can't reproduce the way that they can, right, as they can in warmer weather.
sentences.zh: 而如果你住在北极，那里很冷，细菌无法像在温暖天气那样繁殖，对吧？

sentences.en: Now, I'm not a parasitologiSt.
sentences.zh: 现在，我不是寄生虫学家。

sentences.en: So, I hesitate to be honest with my area of expertise.
sentences.zh: 所以，老实说，我对我的专业领域之外的问题持谨慎态度。

sentences.en: But that is my understanding.
sentences.zh: 但这就是我的理解。

sentences.en: But that's kind of what we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 但这正是我们所谈论的。

sentences.en: There's just, you know, more of these harmful bugs, parasites of one sort or another.
sentences.zh: 只是，你知道，有更多这些有害的虫子，各种各样的寄生虫。

sentences.en: Just more of them can thrive in hotter, wetter places.
sentences.zh: 在更热、更潮湿的地方，它们能繁衍得更多。

sentences.en: So, do you think that some of this behavioral immune system behavior, particularly around xenophobia and prejudice, is playing out now during the COVID pandemic?
sentences.zh: 那么，你认为这种行为免疫系统行为，特别是在仇外心理和偏见方面，现在在新冠大流行期间是否正在发挥作用？

sentences.en: Are people becoming more conformist or less so?
sentences.zh: 人们变得更墨守成规还是更不墨守成规了？

sentences.en: I mean, the news would tell us that people don't want to get vaccinated.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，新闻会告诉我们人们不想接种疫苗。

sentences.en: And yet, as you see the numbers creep up and more vaccine becomes available, people are getting vaccinated.
sentences.zh: 然而，随着你看到数字上升，更多的疫苗变得可用，人们正在接种疫苗。

sentences.en: So, you know, what's at play here?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这里面有什么因素在起作用？

sentences.en: Well, that's a great question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: And it's a complicated question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个复杂的问题。

sentences.en: Because people have particular groups that they seem especially more willing to conform to.
sentences.zh: 因为人们有特定的群体，他们似乎特别愿意顺从这些群体。

sentences.en: So, let me go back to the broader question that you asked about whether these kind of phenomena in general seem to be playing out in the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 所以，让我回到你问的关于这些现象在一般情况下是否似乎在大流行中发挥作用的更广泛的问题。

sentences.en: And it is an empirical question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个实证问题。

sentences.en: I'm a scientist, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，我是一名科学家。

sentences.en: So, it's like, I want to see the data.
sentences.zh: 所以，就像是，我想看到数据。

sentences.en: And there have been a lot of people who have been collecting data of one sort or another, bearing on these kind of questions over the last year.
sentences.zh: 在过去的一年里，有很多人一直在收集各种各样的数据，与这些问题有关。

sentences.en: And some of those results are now appearing in academic journals.
sentences.zh: 其中一些结果现在正出现在学术期刊上。

sentences.en: And there is evidence that some of these things that we've seen in artificial psychology experiments are playing out in the real world.
sentences.zh: 有证据表明，我们在人工心理学实验中看到的一些现象正在现实世界中上演。

sentences.en: So, for instance, early on in the pandemic, political scientists collected data that was looking at whether the pandemic, the onset of the pandemic,
sentences.zh: 例如，在大流行初期，政治学家收集了数据，观察大流行、大流行的爆发，

sentences.en: was affecting Americans' attitudes toward folks from China specifically, toward Asian Americans, toward immigrants more broadly.
sentences.zh: 是否正在影响美国人对来自中国的人、对亚裔美国人、对更广泛的移民的态度。

sentences.en: And they found evidence that it was that these more xenophobic responses were being heightened by the onset of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 他们发现了证据，表明这些更具仇外心理的反应确实因大流行的爆发而加剧了。

sentences.en: There is some work that I saw recently that some psychologists,
sentences.zh: 我最近看到一些心理学家做了一些工作，

sentences.en: an international team of psychologists collected data in Poland that showed that the pandemic was associated with the increased endorsement of very traditional attitudes,
sentences.zh: 一个国际心理学家团队在波兰收集的数据显示，大流行与对非常传统态度的支持增加有关，

sentences.en: including more negative attitudes to people who violated traditional sexual norms and things like that.
sentences.zh: 包括对违反传统性规范的人持更负面的态度等等。

sentences.en: So, in various different places,
sentences.zh: 所以，在不同的地方，

sentences.en: we are seeing evidence that some of these phenomena that we just talked about are being exaggerated because of the fact that at a broad population-wide, worldwide level,
sentences.zh: 我们正在看到证据，表明我们刚才谈到的一些现象正在被夸大，因为在广泛的人口层面、全球层面，

sentences.en: the pandemic is making the threat of disease just kind of extra salient for people in general.
sentences.zh: 大流行使疾病的威胁对人们来说变得格外突出。

sentences.en: And people are just in general feeling more vulnerable and people are just in general feeling more vulnerable to the threat of infection.
sentences.zh: 人们普遍感到更容易受到伤害，人们普遍感到更容易受到感染威胁。

sentences.en: And it's having these social consequences.
sentences.zh: 它正在产生这些社会后果。

sentences.en: There's also research that suggests that the behavioral immune system may influence our choice of mates and our romantic and sexual behavior.
sentences.zh: 还有研究表明，行为免疫系统可能会影响我们的配偶选择以及我们的浪漫和性行为。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that research, too?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈那项研究吗？

sentences.en: I mean, that just sounds fascinating.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这听起来太迷人了。

sentences.en: How does that happen?
sentences.zh: 这是怎么发生的？

sentences.en: Well, it's a great question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: And in fact, some of the first work that people did in this general line of work looked at its effects on people's mate preferences and attraction and so forth.
sentences.zh: 事实上，人们在这一研究领域所做的最早的一些工作，研究了它对人们配偶偏好和吸引力等方面的影响。

sentences.en: So, one line of work looks at physical attractiveness and the extent to which people prioritize physical attractiveness in a potential mate.
sentences.zh: 所以，其中一个研究方向是观察身体吸引力，以及人们在潜在配偶中优先考虑身体吸引力的程度。

sentences.en: And work shows that in places, for instance, where diseases have historically been more prevalent, people place a higher priority on physical attractiveness.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，例如在历史上疾病更普遍的地方，人们对身体吸引力的优先考虑程度更高。

sentences.en: So, why might that be?
sentences.zh: 那么，这可能是为什么呢？

sentences.en: And the answer, there's a couple of answers possible.
sentences.zh: 答案是，有几个可能的答案。

sentences.en: One is that, generally speaking, physical attractiveness serves as kind of a quick and dirty proxy for health.
sentences.zh: 其一是，总的来说，身体吸引力可以作为一种快速且粗略的健康指标。

sentences.en: That is, when people are sick, it affects their appearance in a variety of ways.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，当人们生病时，它会以各种方式影响他们的外表。

sentences.en: And in general, people find less attractive.
sentences.zh: 而且总的来说，人们会觉得（生病的人）吸引力较低。

sentences.en: So, even among folks who are healthy, there's a tendency to just kind of view physical attractiveness as kind of a proxy for health.
sentences.zh: 所以，即使在健康的人群中，也有一种倾向，即把身体吸引力视为一种健康指标。

sentences.en: And in addition to that, people have argued it can also perhaps serve as a proxy for the idea that this person is going to be producing healthy children.
sentences.zh: 此外，人们还认为它也可以作为一种指标，表明这个人将能生育健康的后代。

sentences.en: So, for a variety of reasons, the argument is that when people, when diseases are more prevalent or when people are more freaked out by the threat of disease,
sentences.zh: 所以，出于各种原因，论点是当人们，当疾病更普遍或当人们对疾病威胁感到更恐慌时，

sentences.en: they place a higher priority on physical attractiveness.
sentences.zh: 他们会把身体吸引力放在更高的优先级。

sentences.en: There's other ways in which the behavioral immune system can affect people's inclinations, their romantic inclinations.
sentences.zh: 行为免疫系统影响人们倾向、浪漫倾向的方式还有其他方面。

sentences.en: There's intimate sexual behavior and just intimate social contact in general poses an interesting dilemma for folks because, on the one hand, we get a lot of benefits from it.
sentences.zh: 亲密的性行为和一般的亲密社交接触对人们来说构成了一个有趣的困境，因为一方面，我们从中获得了很多好处。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But, on the other hand, it makes us more vulnerable to the kinds of diseases that people might spread amongst themselves.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，它使我们更容易受到人们可能在彼此之间传播的疾病的侵害。

sentences.en: So, there's this kind of constant tradeoff.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一种持续存在的权衡。

sentences.en: And the idea is that people will resolve that tradeoff somewhat differently depending upon whether they are or are not feeling worried about the threat of infectious disease.
sentences.zh: 其核心观点是，人们是否担心传染病的威胁，会以不同的方式影响他们对这种权衡的取舍。

sentences.en: When people do feel more vulnerable to infectious disease, the idea is that they'll just pull back a little bit from these romantic inclinations.
sentences.zh: 当人们感到更容易受到传染病威胁时，他们往往会稍微收敛一下浪漫倾向。

sentences.en: And there's research that shows that people are just less likely to pursue romantic opportunities when they're feeling more worried about disease.
sentences.zh: 有研究表明，当人们对疾病感到担忧时，他们追求浪漫机会的可能性确实会降低。

sentences.en: And it's not just in the realm of romance, either, for that matter.
sentences.zh: 而且，不仅是在浪漫领域，其他方面也是如此。

sentences.en: There's work that shows that people, just in general, are less socially gregarious when they're worried about infectious diseases.
sentences.zh: 有研究显示，人们在担心传染病时，普遍会减少社交活动。

sentences.en: Because, after all, it's not just intimate sexual contact that poses a risk, but close interpersonal contact in general does.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，不仅是亲密的性接触存在风险，一般的人际密切接触也同样存在风险。

sentences.en: And so, for the same reasons, close interpersonal contact has this tradeoff.
sentences.zh: 因此，出于同样的原因，密切的人际接触也存在这种权衡。

sentences.en: There's lots of benefits from hanging out with friends, from meeting new people and so forth.
sentences.zh: 与朋友聚会、结识新朋友等有很多好处。

sentences.en: But it also carries this risk of disease transmission.
sentences.zh: 但这也带来了疾病传播的风险。

sentences.en: Consequently, when people are more worried about the threat of disease, they tend to just kind of pull back from social contact.
sentences.zh: 因此，当人们更担心疾病威胁时，他们往往会倾向于减少社交接触。

sentences.en: Let's talk for a minute about the role of disgust and how that fits into our behavioral immune system.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈厌恶感的作用，以及它如何融入我们的行为免疫系统。

sentences.en: It obviously plays an important role for us as living beings.
sentences.zh: 作为生命体，它显然对我们起着重要作用。

sentences.en: But what role is that?
sentences.zh: 但那是什么作用呢？

sentences.en: What is the purpose of disgust?
sentences.zh: 厌恶感的目的是什么？

sentences.en: A lot of people have studied disgust for a lot of years and have suggested a variety of roles that disgust plays.
sentences.zh: 许多人多年来一直在研究厌恶感，并提出了它所扮演的多种角色。

sentences.en: And the idea that this emotional experience that we call disgust has evolved.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为厌恶感的这种情感体验是进化而来的。

sentences.en: So, for instance, one expert on disgust has suggested that, really, a long time ago, evolutionarily speaking,
sentences.zh: 例如，一位厌恶感专家曾提出，从进化角度来看，很久以前，

sentences.en: disgust or some early version of disgust, distaste, served a function of just keeping potentially contaminated foodstuffs out of our mouth.
sentences.zh: 厌恶感或其早期形式——反感，其功能仅仅是防止潜在的受污染食物进入我们的口中。

sentences.en: And since it's through our mouth that a lot of potential infections can happen.
sentences.zh: 因为很多潜在的感染都是通过口腔发生的。

sentences.en: And over time, particularly as our ancestors evolved into more and more of kind of a social species,
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，特别是当我们的祖先进化成一种越来越社会化的物种时，

sentences.en: disgust kind of evolved and took on a kind of a broader role that we would not just –
sentences.zh: 厌恶感也随之进化，并承担了更广泛的角色，我们不仅仅是——

sentences.en: it didn't just serve as a way of alerting us to the threat of, you know, contaminated foodstuffs,
sentences.zh: 它不仅仅是一种提醒我们注意受污染食物威胁的方式，

sentences.en: but as kind of a first alert system for the threat of anything that might be contaminating or infectious.
sentences.zh: 而是作为一种针对任何可能具有污染性或传染性威胁的预警系统。

sentences.en: And so what disgust does in folks nowadays, it really, like many emotions, it serves as kind of an alarm system.
sentences.zh: 所以，厌恶感在当今人们身上所起的作用，就像许多情绪一样，它是一种警报系统。

sentences.en: It's essentially in a really powerful, immediate way is alerting me to here's a potential threat of infection and it's leading me to respond in an avoidant way.
sentences.zh: 它本质上是以一种非常强大、直接的方式提醒我这里存在潜在的感染威胁，并引导我采取回避反应。

sentences.en: You've talked about evolution a little bit as we've been chatting here,
sentences.zh: 我们在聊天时已经谈到了一些进化问题，

sentences.en: and I'm wondering over the long term, do you think this pandemic is going to change people's behavior in any lasting way?
sentences.zh: 我想知道从长远来看，你认为这次大流行会在持久层面上改变人们的行为吗？

sentences.en: I think it would be probably silly of me to speculate upon in terms of whether this will actually have evolutionary consequences.
sentences.zh: 我想如果我推测这是否会产生真正的进化后果，那可能有点愚蠢。

sentences.en: But rather, I think where one is likely to see it is in terms of kind of not genetic evolution,
sentences.zh: 但我认为，我们更有可能看到的是——不是基因进化，

sentences.en: but cultural evolution, that the pandemic is likely to have some lasting effects on what kinds of norms govern how people interact with each other.
sentences.zh: 而是文化进化，即大流行很可能会对规范人们互动方式的准则产生持久影响。

sentences.en: And I'm sure I'll be wrong about some of this because I've learned from sad experience that it's really hard to predict the future.
sentences.zh: 我相信我的一些看法会是错的，因为惨痛的经验告诉我，预测未来真的很难。

sentences.en: But I wouldn't be surprised if the tendency for people to be, you know, concerned about being in densely populated, close physical spaces,
sentences.zh: 但如果人们对处于人口稠密、物理距离紧密的空间感到担忧，我一点也不会感到惊讶，

sentences.en: people will be a little bit more resistant for some chunk of time in the future to going into these kind of crowded places.
sentences.zh: 在未来的某段时间里，人们会对进入这些拥挤的地方产生更多的抵触情绪。

sentences.en: So the era of mosh pits may be over.
sentences.zh: 所以，冲撞舞（mosh pit）的时代可能要结束了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, you know, this is why I think it's hard to speculate.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，这就是为什么我认为很难推测的原因。

sentences.en: People have short memories, right?
sentences.zh: 人们的记性很短，对吧？

sentences.en: We'll still do stupid things.
sentences.zh: 我们还是会做蠢事。

sentences.en: And, you know, so I may be less likely personally to dive into a mosh pit two years from now, but my kids might still be moshers in the future.
sentences.zh: 所以，两年后我个人可能不太会跳进冲撞舞池，但我的孩子们将来可能还是会去跳。

sentences.en: I think it's really an interesting question because it gets back to this idea that a lot of the things that help serve as buffers against the spread of disease
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常有趣的问题，因为它回到了这个观点，即许多有助于缓冲疾病传播的事物，

sentences.en: are also taken away things that people value, like close interaction.
sentences.zh: 同时也剥夺了人们所珍视的东西，比如亲密的互动。

sentences.en: And so I think that because there is such a power, people do have such a powerful need for social contact and so forth, that that probably will recover.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，因为人们对社交接触等有着如此强烈的需求，这种需求很可能会恢复。

sentences.en: What I do expect, or at least I'm very interested in seeing this, is the extent to which there will be kind of more of a persistent norm of wearing masks.
sentences.zh: 我所期待的，或者至少我非常有兴趣观察的是，佩戴口罩这一规范在多大程度上会持续下去。

sentences.en: You know, in many parts of the world, people well before the COVID pandemic tended to wear cloth masks over their faces as a way of helping to, you know, prevent the spread of,
sentences.zh: 你知道，在世界许多地方，早在新冠大流行之前，人们就倾向于戴布口罩，以此作为帮助预防，你知道，

sentences.en: you know, just seasonal flu and colds and things like that.
sentences.zh: 预防季节性流感、感冒之类疾病的一种方式。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so now that's, you know, that may persiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以现在，你知道，这可能会持续下去。

sentences.en: We can't say it's a norm with everyone everywhere, but it has become much more of a norm worldwide.
sentences.zh: 我们不能说这在世界各地对每个人都成了规范，但它确实已成为全球范围内更普遍的规范。

sentences.en: And I'm sure that when the pandemic is over, there will be a lot of folks who will be happy to throw their masks away and want to never touch them again.
sentences.zh: 我相信当大流行结束时，会有很多人很高兴扔掉口罩，再也不想碰它们。

sentences.en: But I also bet that there will be a lot of folks who will hang on to their masks and will break them out pretty regularly during cold and flu season.
sentences.zh: 但我敢打赌，也会有很多人会保留他们的口罩，并在感冒和流感季节经常拿出来戴。

sentences.en: And it's likely to have a lot of benefits for public health worldwide.
sentences.zh: 这很可能对全球公共卫生有很多好处。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it has, right?
sentences.zh: 我是说，确实有好处，对吧？

sentences.en: The seasonal flu numbers have been way down this year, so it's absolutely working.
sentences.zh: 今年的季节性流感病例大幅下降，所以它绝对有效。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, last question.
sentences.zh: 好吧，最后一个问题。

sentences.en: What do you think are the most important questions about the behavioral immune system that remain to be answered?
sentences.zh: 你认为关于行为免疫系统还有哪些最重要的问题有待解答？

sentences.en: What else are you working on?
sentences.zh: 你还在研究什么？

sentences.en: I can't say I'm working on this.
sentences.zh: 我不能说我正在研究这个。

sentences.en: I'll speak more broadly on the kinds of things that folks in the broader research community are working on.
sentences.zh: 我会更广泛地谈谈整个研究界正在研究的课题。

sentences.en: And what folks are likely to be working on.
sentences.zh: 以及人们可能正在研究的内容。

sentences.en: I think one really interesting question goes back to how we opened in talking about that not only is there a behavioral immune system that helps us from beginning to getting sick in the first place,
sentences.zh: 我认为一个非常有趣的问题回到了我们开篇所谈到的，不仅存在一种帮助我们从一开始就避免生病的行为免疫系统，

sentences.en: but there's also the real immune system, these immunological defenses that fight off infections when they do get inside us.
sentences.zh: 而且还存在真正的免疫系统，即当感染进入我们体内时，这些免疫防御机制会对抗感染。

sentences.en: And a really interesting question is the extent to which these two different kinds of immune systems actually talk to each other, how they interact.
sentences.zh: 一个非常有趣的问题是，这两种不同的免疫系统在多大程度上真正地相互沟通，它们是如何相互作用的。

sentences.en: And there is various hints of work that do suggest that they are related and they're not just fully independent.
sentences.zh: 有一些研究迹象表明它们是相关的，并非完全独立。

sentences.en: So I'll just, I'll give you, I'll give you two examples.
sentences.zh: 所以我给你，我给你举两个例子。

sentences.en: One example comes from some work that folks have done that shows that when people actually are actually immunologically suppressed,
sentences.zh: 一个例子来自一些研究，这些研究表明，当人们实际上处于免疫抑制状态时，

sentences.en: that their immune system just isn't working as well, those folks compared to other folks tend to show more xenophobic responses to foreigners and things like that.
sentences.zh: 也就是说他们的免疫系统工作得不够好，与其他人群相比，这些人往往对外国人表现出更多的排外反应等。

sentences.en: The idea being that when people actually are immunocompromised, they compensate by ramping up the behavioral immune system.
sentences.zh: 其观点是，当人们免疫功能受损时，他们会通过加强行为免疫系统来进行补偿。

sentences.en: And here's another example that some colleagues and I did a study on this and some other folks have done similar studies that shows that when people perceive things that pose a threat of infection in their environment,
sentences.zh: 这是另一个例子，我和一些同事做过这方面的研究，其他人也做过类似的研究，表明当人们感知到环境中存在感染威胁时，

sentences.en: or when, or when, let's say we look at disgusting pictures, that it actually tends to ramp up our actual immunological defenses.
sentences.zh: 或者当，或者当，比方说我们看令人厌恶的图片时，它实际上往往会增强我们真正的免疫防御能力。

sentences.en: People who do psychoneuroimmunology have known for years that any kind of stressful event can ramp up our immunological defenses.
sentences.zh: 研究心理神经免疫学的人多年来一直知道，任何压力事件都能增强我们的免疫防御能力。

sentences.en: But even more so than encountering other stressful things, for instance, even more so than looking at pictures that scare the hell out of me.
sentences.zh: 但比起遇到其他压力事件，例如，甚至比起看那些让我吓得要死的图片，这种影响更显著。

sentences.en: If I look at pictures of people who themselves look sick, that tends to lead my, my white blood cells to mount a stronger immunological defense against infections.
sentences.zh: 如果我看到看起来生病的人的照片，这往往会促使我的白细胞产生更强的免疫防御来对抗感染。

sentences.en: So it's a different part of the body that's reacting.
sentences.zh: 所以这是身体的不同部位在做出反应。

sentences.en: It's not like a cortisol level, it's white blood cells.
sentences.zh: 这不像皮质醇水平，这是白细胞。

sentences.en: So it really is immune suppressing.
sentences.zh: 所以它确实是免疫抑制的。

sentences.en: It's not just a stress response.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是一种压力反应。

sentences.en: It actually is an immunological response.
sentences.zh: 它实际上是一种免疫反应。

sentences.en: So, I mean, these are some really interesting hints of the, of how these different kinds of mechanisms, these immunological mechanisms,
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，这些都是非常有趣的线索，说明这些不同类型的机制，这些免疫机制，

sentences.en: these psychological mechanisms are in some way deeply connected.
sentences.zh: 这些心理机制在某种程度上是如何深度连接的。

sentences.en: And, and some folks have suggested, hey, you know, it probably makes sense to talk about this as all part of the, the body's integrated means of,
sentences.zh: 而且，有些人建议，嘿，你知道，把这些都看作是身体综合防御手段的一部分是有道理的，

sentences.en: of defending against infectious diseases.
sentences.zh: 即防御传染病的手段。

sentences.en: And within an evolutionary framework, it, it, it, it makes sense that these things would all be kind of deeply connected in some way.
sentences.zh: 在进化框架内，这些事物在某种程度上深度连接在一起是合乎逻辑的。

sentences.en: So a really interesting line of work, and I think it'll take years of, of work ahead is to kind of sort out how,
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常有趣的研究方向，我认为还需要多年的工作来梳理清楚，

sentences.en: how the behavioral immune system interacts with the real immune system.
sentences.zh: 行为免疫系统是如何与真正的免疫系统相互作用的。

sentences.en: So, so that's just one example of something I think is going to be really important and interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以，这只是我认为非常重要且有趣的一个例子。

sentences.en: Well, thank you for joining us today, Dr. Schau.
sentences.zh: 好的，感谢您今天加入我们，Schau博士。

sentences.en: This has been really interesting.
sentences.zh: 这真的非常有趣。

sentences.en: I think you've given us a lot to think about as we make our way through the pandemic and flu season and the whole winter.
sentences.zh: 我想在我们经历大流行、流感季节和整个冬天的过程中，你给了我们很多值得思考的东西。

sentences.en: I appreciate you spending time with us today.
sentences.zh: 感谢您今天抽出时间陪伴我们。

sentences.en: It's been a pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: You can find previous episodes of Speaking of Psychology on our website at speakingofpsychology.org or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 您可以在我们的网站 speakingofpsychology.org 或您获取播客的任何地方找到《心理学谈话》的往期节目。

sentences.en: If you have comments or ideas for future podcasts, you can email us at speakingofpsychology at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 如果您有任何评论或对未来播客的想法，可以发送电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.en: That's speakingofpsychology, all one word, at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 即 speakingofpsychology，连在一起，@apa.org。

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology is produced by Lee Weinerman.
sentences.zh: 《心理学谈话》由 Lee Weinerman 制作。

sentences.en: Our sound editor is Chris Kondayan.
sentences.zh: 我们的音效编辑是 Chris Kondayan。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢您的收听。

sentences.en: For the American Psychological Association,
sentences.zh: 代表美国心理学会，

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是 Kim Mills。
